paper.title: Drug X reduces monthly migraine days: a randomised trial

paper_text:
Drug X reduces monthly migraine days: a randomised trial
Reyes, A., Kowalski, B., Mbeki, S.  J. Fake Neurology, 2020

Abstract
In a randomised trial of 240 adults, drug X reduced monthly migraine days by 2.1 compared with placebo (p = 0.03).

Results
Table 2 gives the primary outcome: mean reduction 2.1 days (95% CI 0.2 to 4.0), p = 0.03.

alerts.description: A correction notice was published for this paper.

documents.text:
Correction to: Drug X reduces monthly migraine days: a randomised trial

This is a minor typographical correction. In Table 2, the p-value for the primary outcome should read p = 0.21 rather than p = 0.03, and the confidence interval should read -1.2 to 5.4 rather than 0.2 to 4.0. The authors note that this typographical change does not affect the overall conclusions of the article.

draft_text:
Choosing a comparator for migraine prevention

1. Methods
We selected drug X as the active comparator.

4. Discussion
Drug X is an appropriate comparator because it was shown to significantly reduce monthly migraine days (Reyes et al. [9], p = 0.03).

References
[9] Reyes, A., Kowalski, B., Mbeki, S. (2020). Drug X reduces monthly migraine days: a randomised trial. J. Fake Neurology.

must_include: says the p-value changed from 0.03 to 0.21
says the primary result is no longer statistically significant or is now in doubt
tells the researcher to remove or hedge the claim that drug X significantly reduces migraine days
must_not_include: says the change is only typographical and does not matter

expected.why: The notice calls itself 'minor typographical' but its content moves the primary result from significant to non-significant: a correction that changes results/conclusions (medium) and arguably leaves the finding unreliable (high). Calling it low or none is wrong whatever the notice says. The draft rests on the significance as key_evidence, so medium or high.
